chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a concubine of a Christian who converts to Islam: Does the Muslim marry her? He said, 'Yes, and her waiting period (iddah) from the Christian is, upon her conversion, the waiting period of a free divorced woman: three months or three menstrual periods. If her waiting period expires, let him marry her if she wishes.'

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine (female slave with whom the master has had intercourse, who becomes free upon his death)
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْحُرَّةِ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The waiting period of a free divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a Christian concubine who converts to Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that upon her conversion, the Christian concubine's iddah transitions to that of a free divorced woman (three months or three cycles), reflecting the juristic principle that her previous status as a slave does not preclude her from the standard waiting period for marriage. This ruling ensures her legal independence is recognized before the owner can marry her, emphasizing the voluntary nature of the union post-iddah. The hadith highlights the interplay between manumission, conversion, and marital eligibility in Shia fiqh.
